analysis: Examined LaunchAgent.swift (head lines 265-270, 287-298) and the benchmark report test. The PR adds two engine-tuning env keys (EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey) to the inferencePassthroughEnvKeys allowlist. passthroughEnvKeys concatenates that list, and passthroughEnvironment (lines 327-348) copies only non-empty values into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables. The allowlist stays fixed and small, and no secrets, tokens, or arbitrary keys are forwarded. The worker opt-in handling and the memory-availability canonicalization are unchanged. These are performance and geometry knobs (prefill chunk and step token budget) set by the local operator. The operator is already inside the TB-003 trust boundary and can set any env or edit the plist. The knobs affect scheduling and memory, not attestation, E2E encryption, cache scoping, or the SSD prefix cache's at-rest crypto (T-041). Residual consideration, not a finding: wide prompt geometry could raise transient memory or GPU pressure (T-029-style availability) if an operator opts in. That is an operator-controlled availability trade-off. The definitions of prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey, and how EngineV2Factory validates and bounds the values, are outside the supplied evidence. I did not check whether it clamps out-of-range values or whether the Gemma 4 default geometry change (the 'wide' default implied by the comments) is safe under memory guards. The test change only adds report schema v5 fields (prefillChunkTokens, maxBatchedTokensPerStep) and a back-compat decode check for schema 4. It has no security impact. Unchanged callers, including WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys, were not examined. Whether the watchdog must also forward these keys is a consistency question, not a security one.
